([[Chantilly, Virginia]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 42 | draft_team = [[New York Knicks]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team1 = [[New York Knicks]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = →[[Westchester Knicks]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team3 = [[Iowa Wolves]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team4 = [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years5 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team5 = [[Miami Heat]] | years6 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team6 = →Sioux Falls Skyforce | highlights = * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Rookie Team (2022) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2021) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|LTU}}}} }} '''Trevor Jamaal Keels''' (born August 26, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Keels was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[shooting guard]]s in the 2021 class. As of September 2026 he is a reserve for the Lithuania Men’s National Team for the upcoming 2027 FIBA World Cup as a neutralized citizen. ==High school career== Keels played basketball for [[Paul VI Catholic High School]] in [[Chantilly, Virginia]], where he was teammates with his future college teammate [[Jeremy Roach]].{{cite web |last=Marks |first=Brendan |title=5-star combo guard Trevor Keels will join friend Jeremy Roach, giving Duke a lethal backcourt |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2495505/2021/04/02/5-star-combo-guard-trevor-keels-will-join-friend-jeremy-roach-giving-duke-a-lethal-backcourt/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=April 2, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 15.6 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game, earning [[Washington Catholic Athletic Conference]] (WCAC) Co-Player of the Year honors.{{cite web |last=Ricardo |first=Chad |title=Paul VI's Trevor Keels already has accomplished a lot, but his story is just beginning |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/high-school/paul-vis-trevor-keels-already-has-accomplished-lot-his-story-just-beginning |website=[[NBC Sports]] |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=July 20, 2020}} In his junior season, Keels led Paul VI to the Virginia Independent Schools Athletic Association Division I state title.{{cite news |last=Errigo |first=Michael |title=After falling short in WCAC, Paul VI boys take home VISAA title |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/highschools/after-falling-short-in-wcac-paul-vi-boys-take-home-visaa-title/2020/02/29/44e8c762-5b39-11ea-9b35-def5a027d470_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=February 29, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 28.7 points, 9.1 rebounds, 7.2 assists and 3.8 steals per game. He was named Virginia [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and was selected to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] rosters.{{cite web |last=Rowe |first=Adam |date=June 4, 2021 |title=Duke signee Trevor Keels named Gatorade Virginia Boy's Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/trevor-keels-duke-blue-devils-virginia-state-award-gatorade-166106883/ |access-date=June 19, 2021 |website=[[247Sports]]}} ===Recruiting=== Keels received his first [[NCAA Division I]] scholarship offer from [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], three games into his high school career.{{cite news |last=Pell |first=Samantha |title=This freshman's high school career is three games old, and he already has a college offer |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2017/12/14/this-freshmans-high-school-career-is-three-games-old-and-he-already-has-a-college-offer/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=June 19, 2021 |date=December 14, 2017}} He finished as a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top [[shooting guard]]s in the 2021 class. On April 2, 2021, Keels committed to playing college basketball for [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] over offers from [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |authorlink2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=April 2, 2021 |title=Trevor Keels commits to Duke, giving Blue Devils three five-stars in 2021 basketball class |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31184121 |access-date=June 18, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2021}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Trevor Keels | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Clinton, MD]] | highschool = [[Paul VI Catholic High School|Paul VI Catholic]] (VA) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = April 2, 2021 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 90 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2021 | rivals ref title = Duke 2021 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2021 Duke Blue Devils Recruiting Class | rivals school = duke | scout s = | espn schoolid = 150 | 247 overall = 22 | rivals overall = 22 | espn overall = 23 | accessdate = September 22, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his collegiate debut, a 79–71 win against [[2021–22 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]], Keels scored 25 points.{{cite news |title=Coach K wins Garden finale as Duke tops Kentucky 79-71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401369850 |access-date=November 10, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2021}} He averaged 11.5 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.7 assists in his first season with Duke. Keels was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Rookie Team.{{cite press release|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} Following his freshman season, Keels announced his intention to enter the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Trevor Keels joins Duke teammates in declaring for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33793753|website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 25, 2022 |date=April 24, 2022}} On June 1, 2022, he announced he would remain in the draft and forego his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=David |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Duke basketball's Trevor Keels will remain in NBA Draft |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/2022/06/01/trevor-keels-not-return-duke-his-sophomore-season/7467186001/|access-date=June 2, 2022 |work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]}} ==Professional career== ===New York / Westchester Knicks (2022–2023)=== Keels was selected with the 42nd overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. On July 10, 2022, Keels signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Knicks.{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Trevor Keels to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-trevor-keels-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}} On February 23, 2023, the Knicks converted his deal to a 10-day contract,{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Trevor Keels to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-trevor-keels-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2023|access-date=February 24, 2023}} which expired on March 5 and he returned to the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Trevor Keels becomes free agent after 10-day contract with Knicks|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2023/03/06/knicks-trevor-keels-10-day-contract-free-agent|work=USA Today|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} On March 12, Keels signed a two-way contract with the New York Knicks.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Sign Trevor Keels to Two-Way Contract|number=1635072198938595328|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=March 12, 2023|access-date=March 12, 2023}} On July 19, 2023, Keels signed another two-way contract with the Knicks,{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title= Trevor Keels Returning To Knicks On Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/07/trevor-keels-returning-to-knicks-on-two-way-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 19, 2023|access-date=July 27, 2023}} but was waived on July 26.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Sign Dylan Windler|number=1684350937035313153|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=July 26, 2023|access-date=July 27, 2023}} ===Iowa Wolves (2023–2025)=== On September 28, 2023, Keels signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Stanton|title=Timberwolves Announce Training Camp Roster and Information|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-announce-training-camp-roster-and-information-3|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2023|access-date=September 28, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}} Nine days later, he joined the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|title=Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} On September 25, 2024, Keels re-signed with the Timberwolves,{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Timberwolves Sign Trevor Keels, Jaedon LeDee, Skylar Mays and Eugene Omoruyi|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-trevor-keels-jaedon-ledee-skylar-mays-and-eugene-omoruyi|website=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} but was waived the next day.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Stanton|title=Timberwolves Waive Trevor Keels|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-trevor-keels|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} On October 25, he rejoined Iowa.{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Iowa Wolves Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Iowa-Wolves/4/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 11, 2024}} ===Miami Heat / Sioux Falls Skyforce (2025–2026)=== On July 28, 2025, Keels' rights were acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web|title=Skyforce Acquires Trevor Keels|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-trevor-keels|access-date=January 27, 2026|website=siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com|language=en}} On January 9, 2026, Keels made all 12 of his three-point attempts and set the G League record for made threes in a game without a miss; he scored a total of 46 points in the game.{{cite news |last=Giles |first=Matt |url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/blue-devils-former-guard-trevor-keels-garners-pro-honor |title=Former Duke Guard Trevor Keels Garners Pro Honor |work=Sports Illustrated |date=2026-01-14 }} He was named Rookie of the Week on January 13. On February 18, 2026, Keels signed a two-way contract with the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web|title=Heat Sign Trevor Keels To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-trevor-keels-to-two-way-contract|access-date=March 22, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
